nodes.title: README — H3 Character Sheet Maker
widgets_values:
# H3 Character Sheet Maker

Turn up to **9 reference images** into a clean six-view character sheet in a single generation.

Feed it a face, an outfit, a weapon and a hat, and H3 will assemble them into one coherent character,
then show you that character from four sides plus two face close-ups.

---

## Why a video model

Six separate image generations of the same character will disagree with each other — the jaw shifts,
the jacket changes, the palette drifts. Six frames from **one** video generation physically cannot,
because they share a single denoising pass.

This workflow renders one continuous 360° orbit, pulls six frames out of it, and stitches them into a
sheet. No hard cuts anywhere, so nothing gets a chance to reinvent itself between shots. The camera
does all the moving; the character stays frozen.

---

## Quick start

1. **Load your references.** Any mix of photos, drawings or anime art. The first one sets the style.
2. **Fill in `Input Text (Prompt)`** — one line per image saying what to take and what to ignore.
3. **Pick your size** on the Resolution Selector: aspect ratio, then megapixels.
4. **Leave duration at 5.** Everything downstream is tuned to it.
5. Queue. The finished sheet lands in `ComfyUI/output/charsheet/`.

---

## The two prompt boxes

They get joined together automatically, so you only ever touch the first one.

**`Input Text (Prompt)`** — yours. Assign every image one job and one ignore list:

```
<Picture 1> - keep the photo style. Use the bald head, facial hair, physique.
<Picture 2> - keep only the black outfit. Remove the hair, remove accessories.
<Picture 3> - use the shield. It is attached to the man's back.
```

Being blunt about what to *ignore* matters as much as what to keep. Backgrounds, poses and the wrong
person's face all travel across unless you rule them out by name.

Describe fabrics and materials **in words** too. Faces carry across on their own; wardrobe drifts.
"Black high-collared coat with silver buckles" survives where "the outfit from `<Picture 2>`" wanders.

**`Prompt for orbiting`** — the fixed half. Backdrop, lighting, lens, the A-pose, the statue lock and
the three beat timings. Leave it alone unless you're changing the shot structure, and if you do, see
*Retiming* below.

---

## What you get

| # | View | Source |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Front | orbit 0% |
| 2 | Left side | orbit 25% |
| 3 | Back | orbit 50% |
| 4 | Right side | orbit 75% |
| 5 | Face, front | beat 2 |
| 6 | Face, three-quarter | beat 3 |

Laid out 3 wide × 2 tall with thin black gutters.

---

## Settings worth knowing

**Duration — leave at 5.** That's 124 frames. Valid lengths are `17n + 5`: 5, 22, 39, 56, 73, 90,
107, 124. Anything else rounds up. 124 puts the orbit at roughly 100°/s, an ordinary turntable speed.
Go much shorter and the spin outruns the model — it smears past about 5° per frame.

**Aspect ratio.** Portrait for people. 9:16 wastes the least frame on a standing figure.

**Megapixels.** 0.5 to scout, 0.7 for normal use, 1.2+ when you want the face crops to hold up. Cost
scales roughly linearly, so prove the composition cheap before you commit.

**Speed-up nodes.** Sage Attention and caching both cost some prompt adherence here. Deliberately left out. Add them if you like.

**Optional outputs.** Two extra save nodes are bypassed by default: every individual frame, and the
raw video. Un-bypass either if you want to cherry-pick your own angles.

---

## Getting good results

**Give it a back view if you have one.** With only front-facing references the entire back of your
character is invented. This is the single biggest quality lever in the workflow, and no amount of
prompt tuning substitutes for it.

**Watch for flutter.** Hair and cloth want to move. The fixed prompt already freezes them hard; if
something still ripples, name the specific offender in your input box.

**Assembling from many sources?** If the character is built from three or more images, consider two
stages: run once to get a clean front view, then feed *that* render back in as `<Picture 1>` and
build the sheet from it. A purpose-made reference beats a pile of contradictory ones.

**Retiming.** The six grab points are locked to the beat timings in the fixed prompt. If you change
those times or the duration, open the subgraph and move the frame indexes to match, or the grabs will
land mid-transition.

---

## Then what

Use the character sheet how you would like. You can input it as a reference for future H3 video generation, use it for custom DnD character, use it for visualizing characters or props.

nodes.title: Exaggerated Expressions
widgets_values:
[STYLE]
The output matches the style of <Picture 1>. Sharp detail on the eyes, brows and mouth. The style never changes and never drifts between shots. No shadows.

[STAGING]
Solid light grey seamless backdrop, one flat uniform tone edge to edge, with no gradient, no vignette, no texture and no floor line. Nothing else is in frame. The subject casts no shadow onto the backdrop and does not sit in its own shadow. Soft form shading on the subject itself is fine and should read its shape. Long telephoto lens, near-orthographic.

Framing is a locked-off portrait from the shoulders to the top of the head: the crown sits just below the top edge of frame, the crop line falls across the shoulders. Face square to camera, eyes into the lens, head level and centred. This framing is identical in every shot — the head never changes size or position in frame.

Only the face changes. The head does not turn, tilt, nod, lean or move at any point. The shoulders and body are completely frozen. There is no wind, no hair movement, no breathing, no sway, no secondary motion of any kind. Lighting is identical in every shot.

Each expression appears fully formed and is then held perfectly still, like a freeze frame. Changes between expressions happen as a single hard snap lasting under 0.1 seconds, with no easing, no blending, no in-between expression, no cut and no dissolve.

[0-0.8 seconds] Expression 1 is already fully formed on the very first frame: HAPPY. Broad genuine smile, mouth corners pulled up and back, cheeks raised, eyes narrowed and crinkled at the outer corners, brows relaxed. Held dead still.

[0.8-1.7 seconds]  Snap to Expression 2: SAD. Inner corners of the brows pulled up and together, upper eyelids drooping, gaze slightly lowered but eyes still open, mouth corners pulled down, chin tightened. Held dead still.

[1.7-2.5 seconds] Snap to Expression 3: LAUGHING. Head-back openmouthed laugh with the head still level and square to camera — eyes fully closed, eyelids curved in happy crescents, cheeks pushed high, mouth wide open with the upper teeth showing, brows raised, nose slightly wrinkled. Held dead still.

[2.5-3.3 seconds] Snap to Expression 4: ANGRY. Brows pulled down and inward with a vertical crease between them, eyes hard and glaring with tense upper lids, lips pressed into a tight line, jaw set. Held dead still.

[3.3-4.2 seconds] Snap to Expression 5: SURPRISED. Brows raised high and curved, forehead creased, eyes wide with white visible above the iris, jaw dropped, mouth open in a loose O. Held dead still.

[4.2-5.0 seconds]   Snap to Expression 6: AFRAID. Brows raised and drawn together, upper lids lifted and lower lids tensed, eyes very wide, lips stretched tight and pulled back horizontally. Held dead still.


[CAMERA] Completely locked off and static for the entire clip. No orbit, no zoom, no push in, no dolly, no pan, no tilt, no roll, no handheld shake, no motion blur, no cuts, no dissolves.
[AUDIO] Silence. No music, no room tone, no voices.

nodes.title: Normal Expressions
widgets_values:
[STYLE]
The output matches the style of <Picture 1>. Sharp detail on the eyes, brows and mouth. The style never changes and never drifts between shots. No shadows.

[STAGING]
Solid light grey seamless backdrop, one flat uniform tone edge to edge, with no gradient, no vignette, no texture and no floor line. Nothing else is in frame. The subject casts no shadow onto the backdrop and does not sit in its own shadow. Soft form shading on the subject itself is fine and should read its shape. Long telephoto lens, near-orthographic.

Framing is a locked-off portrait from the shoulders to the top of the head: the crown sits just below the top edge of frame, the crop line falls across the shoulders. Face square to camera, eyes into the lens, head level and centred. This framing is identical in every shot — the head never changes size or position in frame.

Only the face changes. The head does not turn, tilt, nod, lean or move at any point. The shoulders and body are completely frozen. There is no wind, no hair movement, no breathing, no sway, no secondary motion of any kind. Lighting is identical in every shot.

Every expression is a microexpression: the smallest movement that still reads clearly. Only the brows, eyelids, gaze and mouth corners move, and only slightly. The face underneath stays relaxed and smooth in every shot — no forehead creases, no crow's feet, no crinkling at the corners of the eyes, no deepened lines beside the nose or mouth, no nose wrinkling, no squinting, no bulging or straining. Nothing is exaggerated, theatrical or posed. Eyes stay open and into the lens unless a beat below says otherwise.

Each expression appears fully formed and is then held perfectly still, like a freeze frame. Changes between expressions happen as a single hard snap lasting under 0.1 seconds, with no easing, no blending, no in-between expression, no cut and no dissolve.

[0-0.83 seconds] Expression 1 is already fully formed on the very first frame: GENTLE SMILE. Mouth corners lifted a small amount, lips closed and soft, a quiet warmth in the eyes without narrowing them, eyelids at their normal open position, brows relaxed and level. Skin around the eyes and mouth stays completely smooth. Content and calm, not amused, not beaming. Held dead still.

[0.83-1.67 seconds] Snap to Expression 2: SAD. Inner corners of the brows lifted very slightly, upper eyelids a little heavy, gaze dropped a fraction while the eyes stay open, mouth corners barely turned down, lips closed and soft. Quiet and withdrawn, not crying, not grimacing. Held dead still.

[1.67-2.5 seconds] Snap to Expression 3: LAUGHING. Head level and square to camera. Eyes closed with the lids curved in easy relaxed crescents, mouth open in a natural unforced laugh with the upper teeth showing, brows slightly raised, cheeks softly lifted. Skin stays smooth — no squeezing, no nose wrinkle, no strain. A light amused laugh, mouth only moderately open. Held dead still.

[2.5-3.33 seconds] Snap to Expression 4: ANGRY. Brows lowered slightly and drawn a little inward with no crease forming between them, gaze fixed, steady and cool, faint tension in the upper lids, lips closed and lightly pressed together. Displeased and controlled, not glaring, not snarling, jaw not clenched. Held dead still.

[3.33-4.17 seconds] Snap to Expression 5: SURPRISED. Brows lifted with the forehead staying smooth, eyes a touch wider than normal, lips just parted. Caught off guard for a fraction of a second, not shocked — the jaw does not drop and the eyes do not go wide. Held dead still.

[4.17-5.0 seconds] Snap to Expression 6: CONCERN. Brows drawn slightly together with the inner corners raised a small amount, forehead smooth, eyes fully open, alert and attentive with the gaze level and directly into the lens, lips closed and lightly pressed. Worried about something in front of them, engaged and outward-facing — not sad, not withdrawn, not afraid. Held dead still.

[CAMERA] Completely locked off and static for the entire clip. No orbit, no zoom, no push in, no dolly, no pan, no tilt, no roll, no handheld shake, no motion blur, no cuts, no dissolves.
[AUDIO] Silence. No music, no room tone, no voices.

Face square to camera, eyes into the lens, head level and centred. This framing is identical in every shot — the head never changes size or position in frame.

Only the face changes. The head does not turn, tilt, nod, lean or move at any point. The shoulders and body are completely frozen. There is no wind, no hair movement, no breathing, no sway, no secondary motion of any kind. Lighting is identical in every shot.

Each expression appears fully formed and is then held perfectly still, like a freeze frame. Changes between expressions happen as a single hard snap lasting under 0.1 seconds, with no easing, no blending, no in-between expression, no cut and no dissolve.

[0-0.8 seconds] Expression 1 is already fully formed on the very first frame: ahegao. Eyes rolled upward and strongly cross-eyed, both pupils directed tightly inward toward the bridge of the nose, large amount of white sclera visible below the irises, mouth hanging open, tongue fully out and resting over the lower lip, brows raised and slightly arched. Held dead still.

[0.8-1.7 seconds] Snap to Expression 2: DROOLING FOCUS LOOKING UPWARDS. Eyes locked upward with intense unblinking focus, brows slightly lowered, mouth slightly open, tongue resting on the lower lip with a thin clear trail of drool running from the corner of the mouth. Held dead still.

[1.7-2.5 seconds] Snap to Expression 3: OUT OF BREATH. Heavy-lidded eyes, mouth open, brows relaxed, overall look of being winded and slightly dazed. Held dead still.

[2.5-3.3 seconds] Snap to Expression 4: OPEN-MOUTHED PANT. Heavy-lidded eyes, mouth open in a soft relaxed shape, tongue completely hidden inside the mouth and not visible, brows relaxed. Held dead still.

[3.3-4.2 seconds] Snap to Expression 5: SMUG. One eyebrow raised higher than the other, eyes half-lidded and confident, mouth closed in a small asymmetrical smirk with the corners pulled slightly upward. Held dead still.

[4.2-5.0 seconds]  Snap to Expression 6: COY LIP BITE. Eyes half-lidded and soft, mouth closed, lower lip gently caught between the teeth in a subtle bite, one corner of the mouth pulled slightly upward. Held dead still.

[CAMERA] Completely locked off and static for the entire clip. No orbit, no zoom, no push in, no dolly, no pan, no tilt, no roll, no handheld shake, no motion blur, no cuts, no dissolves.
[AUDIO] Silence. No music, no room tone, no voices.

nodes.title: Note: Speed Patches (PK)
widgets_values:
## Speed Patches — PK / H3 SLA

Chain applies bottom-up on the MODEL. Toggle each group on/off with the bypasser above.

- **1. FP16 Accumulation** (`ModelPatchTorchSettings`): free speed on RTX 30xx+ / most modern GPUs. Safe to leave on.
- **2. LowVRAM Attention** (`MiniMaxLowVRAMAttention`): splits attention into head chunks. Reduces peak VRAM; tiny cost, sometimes a small speedup. Widget: `head_chunks` (default 4).
- **3. Chunk FeedForward** (`MiniMaxChunkFeedForward`): splits FF blocks. Reduces peak VRAM at longer sequence lengths. Widgets: `chunks` (2–4), `seq_threshold` (4096).
- **4. H3 SLA Attention** (`H3SLAAttention`): the big one. Sparse Linear Attention — main speedup. `sparsity_ratio` 0.9 keeps 10% of tokens for very fast, decent-quality; drop to ~0.7 if you see artifacts. `dense_last_steps` controls how many final steps run dense (better quality tail).

### Wiring

Feed the raw `MODEL` from `UNETLoader` into `model`. Take the output `MODEL` to whatever comes next (sampler / patcher).

### Notes

- SLA patches attention — anything else patching attention should sit *before* it in the chain. That is why H3SLAAttention is last.
- `protect_audio=True` avoids audio-latent glitches at some speed cost. Leave on unless testing.
- If the workflow refuses to load, install `comfyui-kjnodes` and `plaguekind-nodes` (H3SLAAttention lives in one of these packs).
